intro: The imperfect describes past habits, ongoing actions, and background.
p.era: I/he/she/you formal was; used to be
p.tenía: I/he/she/you formal had; used to have
p.vivía: I/he/she/you formal lived; used to live
p.iba: I/he/she/you formal went; used to go
p.íbamos: we went; used to go (imperfect of ir)
p.veía: I/he/she/you formal saw; used to see
b1.texto:
The **imperfecto** describes habits, ongoing actions, and background in the past. It presents a situation without focusing on its beginning or end; that situation may have ended later.

- Cuando **era** niño, **vivía** en Lima.
- **Tenía** un perro.
- Siempre **iba** al parque.

Regular endings, in this order — yo, tú, él/ella/usted, nosotros/as, vosotros/as, ellos/ellas/ustedes: **-ar** verbs use -aba, -abas, -aba, -ábamos, -abais, -aban; **-er/-ir** verbs use -ía, -ías, -ía, -íamos, -íais, -ían. The vosotros/as forms are used mainly in Spain; with ustedes, use the third-person plural. The three common irregular verbs are **ser** (era, eras, era, éramos, erais, eran), **ir** (iba, ibas, iba, íbamos, ibais, iban), and **ver** (veía, veías, veía, veíamos, veíais, veían).
b2.titulo: Four useful verbs in the imperfect
b2.nota: The yo form matches él, ella, and usted: yo era, él era, ella era, usted era.
b3.f0: When I was a child, I lived in Lima.
b3.f1: Did you have brothers or sisters?
b3.f3: I always used to go to the park.
b5.pregunta: Complete: when I was a child.
b5.o0.refuerzo: A description in the past uses the imperfect: era.
b5.o1.refuerzo: The indefinido presents a bounded event; era is usual for this childhood description.
b6.traduccion: I always used to go to the park.
b7.pregunta: Complete: I used to have a dog.
b7.o0.refuerzo: A past situation with no end: imperfect.
b7.o1.refuerzo: Tuve would present having the dog as a bounded event or period.
b8.pregunta: Complete: we always went to the park.
b8.o0.refuerzo: A habit in the past: imperfect of ir.
b8.o1.refuerzo: Fuimos presents a completed trip; siempre marks a repeated past habit here.
b9.pregunta: Translate: «When I was a child, I lived in Lima.»
b10.texto:
**The app cannot check this part.** For the writing, please use pen and paper. For the speaking, say it out loud and, if you can, practise with a native speaker or a teacher who can correct you.

**Write (60–80 words).** Describe your childhood: where you lived, what you were like, what you used to do.

**Speak (about 1 minute).** Tell someone what your school was like and what you used to do after class.
